sections.content: How many people are "residential, day and domiciliary care managers and proprietors"?

56,025 people

were counted on the census as "residential, day and domiciliary care managers and proprietors" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Managers and proprietors in this group organise and co-ordinate the resources necessary in the provision and running of residential and day care establishments and domiciliary care services for persons who require specialised care and/or supervision.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "residential, day and domiciliary care managers and proprietors", 15.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "residential, day and domiciliary care managers and proprietors" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "residential, day and domiciliary care managers and proprietors" included:

  • further education teaching professionals
  • health care practice managers
  • registered community nurses

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "residential, day and domiciliary care managers and proprietors" there were more women than men (77.2% compared with 22.8%).

This means "residential, day and domiciliary care managers and proprietors" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "other managers and proprietors".

Men made up 22.8% and women made up 77.2% of "residential, day and domiciliary care managers and proprietors"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "residential, day and domiciliary care managers and proprietors" included:

  • welfare and housing associate professionals (other)
  • exam invigilators
  • welfare professionals (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "residential, day and domiciliary care managers and proprietors" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "residential, day and domiciliary care managers and proprietors" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "residential, day and domiciliary care managers and proprietors", 11.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (86.5% compared with 13.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (89.6%) than self-employed (10.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
